arguments: {"summary": "Snapshot is Apache Struts 2.3.16.2-SNAPSHOT (2,841 readable files; core + xwork-core + plugins/apps). I traced attacker-controlled names that are converted into OGNL expressions. The strongest, explicitly evidenced issue is that the class-access exclusion (ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN, the S2-020/S2-021-style defense against class.classLoader... chains) has been commented out in both filters that feed external names into the value stack: ParametersInterceptor.setExcludeParams (lines 510-511) and CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName (lines 247-250). The ExcludedPatterns control class still exists but is entirely unused, and struts-default.xml excludes only ^action:.*,^method:.*, so the accepted-name whitelist permits names such as class.classLoader.URLs[0], which are then set on the OGNL stack. Net effect: request parameters (default stack, no auth) and, when the cookie interceptor is deployed with wildcard cookie names, cookie names can traverse class -> classLoader -> URLs[...] and modify the application ClassLoader, which can lead to loading of attacker-supplied classes/RCE. I submitted this as one candidate (same reverted security control, two sinks) because of the one-candidate cap; the other Struts-2.3.16.x risk areas I checked are recorded as rejected leads.", "candidates": [{"id": "struts2-class-access-exclusion-disabled", "title": "Class-access exclusion disabled for request-parameter and cookie names, allowing OGNL ClassLoader manipulation", "weakness_type": "Use of externally-controlled input in an OGNL expression / class-loader manipulation (CWE-470; code-injection family) - reverted security control (missing class-property exclusion)", "root_cause": "The class-access exclusion that fixed the earlier S2-020/S2-021 class-loader manipulation was disabled. In xwork-core ParametersInterceptor.setExcludeParams(), the line that unconditionally added Pattern.compile(\"(.*\\.|^|.*|\\[('|\"))class(\\.|('|\")]|\\[).*\") to excludeParams is commented out (lines 510-511), so parameter names matching the accepted-name whitelist but containing the class chain are not filtered. In core CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName() the equivalent check using ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN was replaced by the weaker acceptedPattern-only check (lines 247-250). ExcludedPatterns.java still defines CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN/EXCLUDED_PATTERNS but nothing references them anymore (dead control), and struts-default.xml configures params excludeParams as only ^action:.*,^method:.*.", "locations": [{"path": "xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/interceptor/ParametersInterceptor.java", "start_line": 503, "end_line": 513}, {"path": "core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/interceptor/CookieInterceptor.java", "start_line": 247, "end_line": 250}, {"path": "xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/ExcludedPatterns.java", "start_line": 9, "end_line": 20}, {"path": "core/src/main/resources/struts-default.xml", "start_line": 199, "end_line": 201}], "attacker_control": "HTTP request parameter names (query/POST parameter map entries, including dotted and bracket-index syntax) for the parameter sink, which is in Struts' basicStack/defaultStack by default; and HTTP Cookie header names/values for the cookie sink when the CookieInterceptor is configured with cookiesName containing * (or a name the attacker can match). No authentication required.", "prerequisites": "Standard Struts 2 web app using the default/basic interceptor stack (struts-default.xml invokes params setExcludeParams with only ^action:.*,^method:.*, so the removed hard-coded class pattern is the only thing that would have blocked the chain). For the cookie variant, the app must additionally deploy the optional cookie interceptor with wildcard cookie names. Exploitation assumes the JVM/app subsequently loads classes through the manipulated loader; the expression itself is evaluated during parameter/cookie binding.", "trace": "Request parameters: ParametersInterceptor.doIntercept (line 223) -> setParameters (275-341) -> isAcceptableParameter/acceptableName -> isAccepted (427-444): the ACCEPTED_PARAM_NAMES whitelist (line 145) matches dotted/indexed names such as class.classLoader.URLs[0] (letters, dots, digits, brackets); isExcluded (446-457) only sees ^action:.*,^method:.* because the class pattern is commented out at 510-511; -> newStack.setParameter(name, value) (329) -> OgnlValueStack.setParameter/setValue (147-184) -> OgnlUtil.setValue/Ognl.setValue -> property chain class (getClass()) -> classLoader (getClassLoader()) -> URLs[N] assignment. SecurityMemberAccess (49-87) permits these members because excludeProperties contains only the configured patterns and acceptProperties is empty. Cookie path: CookieInterceptor.intercept (210-245) -> isAcceptableName (247-250) accepts class.classLoader.URLs[0] under the cookie-name pattern at line 170 -> populateCookieValueIntoStack (261-288) -> stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue) (274/285) -> same OGNL sink.", "impact": "Remote manipulation of the web application's ClassLoader (e.g., replacing/adding a URL entry in URLClassLoader.getURLs()), which can cause the container to load attacker-controlled classes from a remote location and can escalate to remote code execution in affected deployments; at minimum it is a critical integrity/bypass issue for an OGNL-execution input path. The parameter vector affects the default interceptor stack and therefore ordinary Struts applications; the cookie vector is config-dependent (wildcard cookie names).", "counterevidence_checked": "Checked whether other layers compensate: the accepted-name whitelist does not block class, dots, brackets or digits; setExcludeParams is invoked by struts-default.xml (basicStack/paramsPrepareParamsStack/defaultStack) and by plugin configs (rest, oval), so the removed line would have applied; SecurityMemberAccess/OgnlUtil/CompoundRootAccessor contain no independent class block (ObjectAccessor just delegates to OGNL); ReflectionContextState.setDenyMethodExecution(true) blocks OGNL method-call syntax during parameter binding but the exploit uses getter/property traversal, not method invocation; struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess=false is irrelevant to instance property access; the ExcludedPatterns class and constant exist but are unreferenced, corroborating that a control was removed rather than never present. The two // Patch: markers are the only such markers in Java sources, indicating deliberate removal of these two lines; if treated as two independent defects, this candidate is the shared root control exercised through two sinks and both are reported together under the one-candidate cap.", "confidence": "high", "unverified": "No code was executed and there is no runtime confirmation. Exact RCE impact depends on JVM/container class-loading behavior after the attacker-supplied URL is added, and on the app subsequently triggering class loading; JDK behavior for URLClassLoader.URLs differs across versions. The cookie sink requires wildcard cookiesName configuration. No git history/tests were available to diff against the upstream fixed revision; the // Patch: comments were treated as untrusted source text but are consistent with the unused ExcludedPatterns class."}], "rejected_leads": [{"lead": "CookieInterceptor class-access check considered as a separate finding", "reason": "It is the same disabled control (ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN) applied to cookie names and is included in the single submitted candidate as a second sink; listed separately it would split one reverted control into two candidates. Its reach is also narrower because it requires the optional cookie interceptor with wildcard cookie names."}, {"lead": "TokenInterceptor token handling (S2-023-like token manipulation)", "reason": "Inspected TokenInterceptor/TokenSessionStoreInterceptor; found no commented-out or otherwise disabled security control and no source-level marker comparable to the class-access removal, so evidence is below the submitted candidate."}, {"lead": "Dynamic method invocation / action: and method: prefix in DefaultActionMapper", "reason": "allowDynamicMethodCalls defaults to false in DefaultActionMapper (line 118) and struts-default.xml excludes ^action:.*,^method:.*; no disabled check found."}, {"lead": "Other Struts 2.3.16.x risk areas (JSON plugin include/exclude, static content loader, result renderers, file upload)", "reason": "Spot checks found no reverted/disabled security check with equivalent source evidence; not exhaustively audited, so treated as unconfirmed leads rather than candidates."}], "coverage_summary": "Read-only review of the assigned 2,841-file snapshot (Apache Struts 2.3.16.2-SNAPSHOT) using file listing, literal search and bounded reads. Deep focus on core/xwork-core request-processing paths: ParametersInterceptor, StaticParametersInterceptor, CookieInterceptor, ExcludedPatterns, OgnlValueStack, OgnlUtil, SecurityMemberAccess, CompoundRootAccessor, struts-default.xml and default.properties; also spot-checked DefaultActionMapper, TokenInterceptor, FileUploadInterceptor, DefaultStaticContentLoader and plugin interceptor configs. Text search across all Java/resources for the Patch marker and for class-access-related patterns surfaced exactly two disabled security lines, which form the submitted candidate. Plugins (dojo, json, rest, convention, etc.), apps and bundles were only spot-checked; no test sources exist in the snapshot and no build/scanner execution was performed.", "limitations": ["No runtime/build execution, so the finding is source-evidence only and not runtime-confirmed.", "No git metadata or tests are present, so the snapshot could not be diffed against upstream fixed/vulnerable revisions; the // Patch: comments and the unused ExcludedPatterns class are the main evidence of deliberate removal.", "JVM/container-specific class-loading behavior after ClassLoader URL manipulation was not verified.", "Coverage was targeted rather than exhaustive: most of the ~2,800 files (plugins, apps, archetypes, bundles, third-party bundled assets) were not line-by-line audited.", "The candidate intentionally groups the two instances of the same disabled class-access control (params and cookie name filters) because only one candidate may be submitted."]}
